messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0001. Outcome: refund_partial $4.17. Recommended action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $4.17 to the rider (NS-7) for the unexcused detour, and note the RD-1 breach on the driver's record for the 2.96 km off-route segment.. Escalated: False.
Reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the fare is metered and extra kilometres feed straight into the fare [F6][RD-2]. The trace records one off-route segment, 09:32–09:38, 2.96 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.00 km [F3][F1], and the driver's only explanation is his post-trip statement that his GPS rerouted him [F8].

RD-4 does not excuse that segment. There is no qualifying traffic incident on the replaced stretch [F11][RD-4], and the speed-band records on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard (band 4, 30–39 km/h) are neither band 1 nor band 2 and in any case cannot exempt a segment on their own [F9][F10][RD-4(b)].

RD-5 does not excuse it either. The chat record between rider and driver is empty [F7], so there is no rider message sent before 09:32 that agrees to any road, area or route the driver named [RD-5]. The driver's statement that he followed his own GPS is not rider consent, and a verbal-agreement claim appearing only in a driver statement does not count [F8][RD-5]. Because the chat record is complete and holds no rider agreement, the segment is not undetermined but counts [RD-5].

RD-3 gives no relief: no stop was measured in the segment and the rider named no place there [F7][RD-3(a)]. The segment is therefore an unexcused detour, and recovery follows RD-2: 2.96 km × $1.41/km = $4.1736, rounded to $4.17 [F3][F6][RD-2]. I decline to refund the difference between the total billed excess and the segment sum (2.96 km of a 3.2 km billed excess), which is the map-matching residual RD-2 leaves untouched [F1][F4][RD-2].

The safety screen raises nothing: there are no chat messages, and the complaint and driver statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. RD-6's account flag is not triggered because the driver has no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days [F14][RD-6], and the rider's own record is immaterial to the amount [F13].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments:
{"rider": "We reviewed your dispute and found the driver took an off-route detour on your trip. The route data shows a 2.96 km stretch driven where the best route needed no extra distance, and nothing in the records supports the driver's reason for it, so that portion of your fare was not justified.

We're issuing a $4.17 Ryde voucher to your account. It's paid as a voucher, not a card refund.

The driver's record will note a route breach. No further action is needed from you.", "driver": "We reviewed a route dispute on one of your trips. The trip data shows a 2.96 km off-route stretch, and the reasons you gave did not account for it, so the extra distance on that stretch was not chargeable.

As a result, the rider's fare for that portion is being refunded as a $4.17 Ryde voucher, and a route breach will be noted on your record.

This does not affect your ability to keep accepting trips. Please follow the suggested route unless the rider agrees to a change during the trip."}
